title: Continuous Security Monitoring Across the Information System
exclusions: This is the continuous-security-monitoring posture control common to FedRAMP SI-4 (system monitoring) and the GLBA Safeguards Rule §314.4(d)(2) (continuous monitoring). It proves monitoring is operating across every in-scope index/feed and surfaces high-severity activity and any monitored feed that has gone quiet. It does NOT cover deep per-surface detection (network UC-22.7.51, auth UC-22.8.41), audit-log generation coverage (UC-22.35.6), or response. Out-of-scope feeds are excluded via the monitored-index inventory.
evidence: Saved search 'UC-22.50.46 — continuous monitoring posture' runs on a short cadence, writes a per-index monitoring record to the restricted audit_evidence index, and feeds the 'Continuous security monitoring' dashboard — the dated evidence a 3PAO (FedRAMP) or qualified assessor (GLBA) reads to confirm continuous monitoring operates without gaps.

compliance.assurance_rationale: FedRAMP SI-4 (inheriting NIST 800-53 SI-4) requires monitoring the information system to detect attacks, indicators of potential attacks and unauthorized activity across the authorization boundary. This UC is the operating posture control: it confirms every in-scope monitored feed is live (no feed gone quiet), surfaces high-severity activity, and produces a dated per-index monitoring record across the boundary. Splunk is the sole-sufficient mechanism evidencing that continuous system monitoring operates, so the grade is full; specific detections (SI-4 enhancements) are layered by the per-surface UCs.

compliance.assurance_rationale: The GLBA Safeguards Rule §314.4(d)(2) requires, in lieu of annual penetration testing plus semi-annual vulnerability assessments, continuous monitoring or periodic testing designed to detect actual and attempted attacks on or intrusions into information systems. This UC is the continuous-monitoring implementation that permits that election: it proves monitoring is operating across every in-scope feed, surfaces high-severity events, and flags any monitored feed that has gone quiet, producing dated evidence. Splunk is the sole-sufficient mechanism evidencing continuous monitoring under §314.4(d)(2), so the grade is full.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=target_index` sourcetype='target_sourcetype' where `entity` satisfies `gap_minutes` > 120 for UC-22.50.46 ('Continuous Security Monitoring Across the Information System'). Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest benign `target_index` / `target_sourcetype` events where `entity` stays below `gap_minutes` > 120, or exclude the test entity via `compliance_exception_register.csv` with a valid window. Confirm zero alert rows for UC-22.50.46.

dataSources: All in-scope security/audit indexes across the authorization boundary (or GLBA information systems), reconciled against the monitored-index inventory lookup `monitored_indexes.csv` (columns `index`, `owner`, `required`). Severity is read from the normalised `severity` field where present. Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: Splunk Enterprise / Splunk Cloud Platform (native). Splunk Enterprise Security optional for notable/risk on high-severity rows. (Splunkbase) — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)
spl:
index=* sourcetype=* (severity=* OR signature=* OR action=*) earliest=-24h
| eval sev=lower(coalesce(severity, "informational"))
| stats count as events, count(eval(match(sev,"(?i)crit|high|sev[12]|emergenc"))) as high_sev, dc(host) as hosts, values(sourcetype) as sourcetypes, latest(_time) as last_event by index
| eval gap_minutes=round((now()-last_event)/60, 1)
| eval monitor_status=case(gap_minutes>120, "STALE - monitored feed quiet >2h", high_sev>0, "high-severity events present", true(), "monitoring")
| eval reviewed_at=strftime(now(), "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S")
| table reviewed_at, index, events, high_sev, hosts, sourcetypes, gap_minutes, monitor_status
| sort monitor_status, - high_sev
description: Operates the continuous-security-monitoring posture control common to FedRAMP SI-4 and the GLBA Safeguards Rule §314.4(d)(2): on a short cadence it confirms every in-scope monitored feed is live, surfaces high-severity activity per index, and flags any feed that has gone quiet — producing a single dated per-index monitoring record an assessor can read.
value: Operates the continuous-security-monitoring posture control common to FedRAMP SI-4 and the GLBA Safeguards.... Timely UC-22.50.46 alerting on 'Continuous Security Monitoring Across the Information System' reduces audit findings, regulatory gaps, and attestation delays before manual triage or audit channels escalate.
implementation: (1) Maintain monitored_indexes.csv as the version-controlled inventory of in-scope feeds (index, owner, required); (2) normalise a `severity` field across sources where possible; (3) schedule on a short cadence (e.g. every 15 minutes) with a daily evidence snapshot; (4) route the per-index record to the restricted audit_evidence index and open a ticket for STALE feeds; (5) tune the freshness budget per feed class. Indexes required: all in-scope monitored indexes; Lookups: monitored_indexes.csv.
visualization: Table (index, owner, events, high_sev, gap_minutes, monitor_status) with STALE/high-severity rows highlighted; single-value '% of in-scope feeds live'; time chart of high-severity events per index. Key fields: `index`, `monitor_status`, `high_sev`.

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Authorised FEDRAMP control testing** — Internal audit exercises 'Continuous Security Monitoring Across the Information System' (UC-22.50.46) on `entity` during scheduled clause SI-4 sampling. Match compliance programme calendar.

2. **External assessor sampling** — QSA activity spikes `index=audit_evidence` `configured sourcetype` without crossing `gap_minutes` > 120. Cross-check engagement letter in `fedramp_exception_register.csv`.

3. **Planned maintenance affecting control telemetry** — CAB change pauses ingestion to `audit_evidence` for `entity`. Compare `_time` with active change record.

4. **Third-party processor under contract** — BAA/DPA-covered vendor generates expected rows grouped by `entity` during normal service delivery.

**Suppression mechanism:** `fedramp_exception_register.csv` keyed on `entity`, `exception_reason`, `valid_until`, joined before alert threshold.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Enterprise ≥9.2 or Splunk Cloud. Splunk Enterprise Security optional for notable/risk on high-severity rows.
• **Monitored-index inventory**: `monitored_indexes.csv` (index, owner, required) is the authoritative scope statement for what 'continuous monitoring' covers — version it in source control.
• **Severity normalisation**: map a `severity` field across sources where attack detection depends on it (CIM alignment).
• **Evidence index**: restricted `audit_evidence` with retention meeting the strictest applicable obligation.
• **Regulatory mapping**: evidences FedRAMP `SI-4` and GLBA `§314.4(d)(2)`. Every result carries `monitor_status` and `reviewed_at`.

## Step 1 — Own the monitored-feed inventory

The posture control can only prove 'continuous' if it knows what should be flowing. Populate monitored_indexes.csv from the authorization-boundary / information-system inventory; set `required=true` for feeds that must always be live and assign a named owner for STALE follow-up. Treat changes as change-controlled — a feed removed here drops out of the coverage denominator.

## Step 2 — Implement the search

The search rolls events per index, counts high-severity events, and derives freshness (`gap_minutes`) from the latest event. `monitor_status` encodes the posture: STALE when a feed is quiet beyond budget, high-severity present, or nominal monitoring. Schedule on a short cadence with a daily snapshot:

```ini
[UC-22.50.46: Continuous Security Monitoring Across the Information System]
cron_schedule = */15 * * * *
dispatch.earliest_time = -24h
dispatch.latest_time = now
actions = summary_index
action.summary_index._name = audit_evidence
action.summary_index.marker = uc=22.50.46,controls=FedRAMP-SI-4;GLBA-314.4d2
```

## Step 3 — Validate

Positive: pause a required feed and confirm a STALE row. Negative: with all feeds live and no high-severity events, confirm all rows show 'monitoring'.

## Step 4 — Operationalize

Build 'Continuous security monitoring': single-value '% of in-scope feeds live', a per-index posture table (STALE/high-severity highlighted), and a high-severity trend. Schedule the daily evidence export to audit_evidence — that is the FedRAMP/GLBA continuous-monitoring artefact.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting and caveats

• **A live feed shows STALE:** its events may be delayed or mis-timestamped; check ingestion latency and the freshness budget for that feed class.

• **No high-severity ever:** confirm the severity field is normalised on sources where it matters.

• **Scope discipline:** reconcile monitored_indexes.csv against the boundary inventory so the posture denominator stays complete.

**Ecosystem integration:** Forward compliance detections to Splunk SOAR for automated incident triage and escalation playbooks. Enrich events with asset context from ServiceNow CMDB. Cross-reference with CrowdStrike Falcon or Microsoft Defender for Endpoint for host forensics and threat detection context. Integrate Okta or Azure AD identity context to determine if the acting user had appropriate authorisation. Feed validated findings into the GRC platform (e.g., RSA Archer, ServiceNow GRC, or AuditBoard) for regulatory compliance tracking and audit evidence management.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (Splunk Enterprise / Splunk Cloud Platform (native). Splunk Enterprise Security optional for notable/risk on high-severity rows. (Splunkbase) — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=see SPL into index=main. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`gap_minutes, high_sev, monitor_status, quiet`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: We keep a master list of every system we're supposed to be watching and check every few minutes that each one is still sending us its security information — and we raise a flag the moment any of them goes quiet, which is exactly what an intruder would try to make happen.
